newsitem.title: UK: FKI to buy Italy's Marelli for 34.8 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: FKI to buy Italy's Marelli for 34.8 mln stg.

text.p: UK engineering manufacturer FKI said on Wednesday it had conditionally agreed to buy Italian low voltage electric motors and alternators manufacturer Nuova Marelli Motori for about 34.8 million stg in cash.
The deal includes the rights on the "Marelli Motori" brand and FKI will take on a loan previously granted by the vendors, U.S. investment funds Mutual Discovery and Wexford Management LLC.
FKI said in a statement it would take on the net financial debt of Marelli which, at June 30, was 17.5 million stg.

"The acquisition of Marelli is expected to be earnings enhancing from the outset, while its planned integration into FKI's Engineering Group will further improve its growth and profitability," FKI stated.

Marelli, whose products include asynchronous AC motors, alternators, DC motors for fork lifts and electric motors for lifts, was founded in 1891 and had won strong brand recognition in the worldwide market for its products, FKI said.
In the year to December 31, 1995, Marelli had consolidated sales of 56.5 million stg and consolidated operating profit of 2.9 million stg after costs of around 3.0 million.
These holding company costs will no longer be payable after the acquisition. The consolidated net assets of the company at December 31, 1995, were 16.7 million stg.
FKI said it expected the acquisition, which is conditional on approval by the Italian Antitrust Authority, to be completed during October.
